key_insight: A deforming particle cloud can be reduced to an ellipsoid-based Lagrangian state whose aspect-ratio evolution is driven by a balance between aligned strain forcing and geometric relaxation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a compact, interpretable diagnostic and reduced-order model for tracking coherent deformation in stochastic incompressible flows and turbulence applications.
method: Release a volume-filled particle cloud and summarize it by the minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid and its inertia tensor.
Coarse-grain the local velocity gradient over the ellipsoid to extract scale, strain, vorticity, and alignment variables.
Identify a physics-informed stochastic generator with a source–sink decomposition, using scale-dependent drivers and a residual feedback closure.
evidence_signal: In 2D isotropic incompressible Gaussian-H"older finite-time-correlated synthetic flow data, the ellipsoid aspect ratio saturated statistically while the perceived gradient showed clear scale dependence and the strain–vorticity balance remained approximately ordinary.
watch_item: The closure is calibrated on synthetic 2D data, so transfer to 3D turbulent flows or real measurements may require re-tuning and validation of the alignment and residual models.
paper_title: Lagrangian Ellipsoid Diagnostics for Stochastic Hydrodynamics: Source--Sink Modeling of Deforming Particle Clouds
